newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says citizens need not flee Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says citizens need not flee Cambodia.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said on Friday there was no need to evacuate Indonesians from Cambodia after recent civil violence as the situation in the country, particularly in the capital Phnom Penh, was improving.
"We will continue to monitor the situation in that country and wait for reports from the Indonesian embassy in Cambodia," Alatas was quoted by the official Antara news agency as saying.
The same report quoted Defence and Security Minister Edi Sudradjat as saying he was ready to fly home Indonesian citizens living in Cambodia. He did not say how many lived there.
Antara quoted Indonesia's mission in Kuala Lumpur as denying what it said was a report in Malaysia that 12 Indonesians had been evacuated there this week.
Several thousand foreigners have left Cambodia since Phnom Penh's battered airport reopened on Tuesday.

Last weekend forces loyal to powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen battled First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's men in the city streets, ousting Ranariddh and leaving 58 dead and up to 200 wounded.
Hun Sen denied staging a coup in the weekend fighting, but the events have led several foreign governments to evacuate their nationals or recommend they leave the country.
Most Western embassies were assuring their nationals that the situation in Cambodia was relatively safe and were careful to call the exodus a voluntary departure and not an evacuation.
